new_statements.rule_in_words: Sherdukpen (both Rupa and Shergaon) has iambic word rhythm: in the typical (prefix+)root word the first syllable is unstressed, short and often reduced to schwa or zero, and stress falls on the second syllable, which is the root; grammatical suffixes are unstressed (Bodt p.300: short suffix rhymes 'conditioned by a lack of stress on these suffixes'). Jacquesson (2015/2018, Rupa) states the same first-hand: non-compound disyllabic nouns carry 'a strong accent on the last syllable' with reduction of the first vowel, and in negated verbs 'the stress or accent is then on the second syllable (the verb root)'. Net: stress on the root = second/last syllable of the prosodic stem; could also be filed as fixed: second syllable/final-of-stem (iambic).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Jacquesson: true compounds keep both syllables full (each syllable pronounced) rather than showing the reduced-first-syllable iambic pattern; s+stop clusters (spu 'cow', stu 'horse') are monosyllables, never restored as CvCV; degree of first-vowel reduction varies by speaker and speech rate (full vowel or echo vowel in slow/elicited speech, Bodt p.171 likewise). Bodt notes a few items retaining a full-vowel prefix, suggesting the trochaic>iambic shift is recent and uneven. Tone: Jacquesson says tones survive only in three small villages and are lost in Rupa; Boro 2024 posits H1/H2/L tones for Rupa; Bodt describes a glottal-constricted rising-pitch vowel series rather than tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (prefix+root+suffix word; elicited citation forms and connected speech both discussed). Bodt's statement is a generalisation over all Sartang and Sherdukpen varieties from his own fieldwork on Rupa and Shergaon; Jacquesson's statements are specific to Rupa (Thong clans) Sherdukpen.
new_statements.identity_note: Bodt 2024's stress statement is framed for 'the Sartang and Sherdukpen varieties' jointly (his Sherdukpen data = Rupa and Shergaon, both under sher1257; Sartang is a separate Glottolog language). Jacquesson 2015/2018 describes Rupa Sherdukpen as spoken by the Thong clans; Boro 2024 also Rupa; Dondrup 1988 reportedly Shergaon. Wikipedia/Glottolog dialects: Rupa (Tukpen) and Shergaon.
